conventions.hubs: An add-on is turned on per account and adds a monthly base fee. Add-ons stack at full price; each includes the production basics, so a business app never needs the Consumer Identity add-on for its branding.
conventions.basics: Production basics come with any add-on: your branding, managed delivery, custom security settings and the higher limits. They have no price of their own, so no add-on's base fee is under $100.
conventions.user_meters: Monthly active users are never billed, and requiring MFA never counts a user. The Consumer Identity add-on counts social users: a user who signs in through an external identity provider set up on a project and not linked to a team, once a month. Password, passkey, magic-link and OTP sign-ins never count. An identity provider linked to a team is an SSO connection, counted by Multi-Tenancy, never twice.
conventions.tiers: Two tiers: Pay as you go and Enterprise. Pay as you go starts free with no card, with every core feature and a free amount on most meters; add-ons go on top. Billing keeps two plan ids for it: free while no add-on is on, pro once one is.
conventions.allowance: Every meter Pay as you go offers before an add-on has a free amount. Turning on the meter's add-on raises it to the add-on's included amount; past that, the price applies.
conventions.invoice: Your bill is the base fees of the add-ons you turned on, plus usage past what they include, plus any extra capacity or support you added. While no add-on is on, nothing is billed.
conventions.caps: Separately from the free amounts, owners can set a monthly budget with alerts at 50, 80 and 100 percent of it. A budget only notifies: it never stops sign-ins or switches security enforcement off.
conventions.preview: While Zitadel's next version is in preview, nothing is billed. An add-on's prices apply once it reaches general availability, and accounts that joined during the preview keep them for 12 months after that.
conventions.roadmap: An add-on turned on now gains its missing features as they ship, at the same price.
conventions.capacity: API requests are never billed. Each project has a rate limit; owners add capacity in steps, which raise every project's limit.
conventions.bot_checks: The built-in bot challenge is free on every account. With any add-on, sign-ins and sign-ups can also be checked with your own CAPTCHA keys (Turnstile, hCaptcha or reCAPTCHA) or a verdict your edge forwards (Vercel BotID, Cloudflare). Such a check counts only when it passes and lets a request through, once per decision: failed checks and refused requests never count, so an attack can't grow the bill.
conventions.self_hosted: Self-hosted Zitadel has the same features, add-ons and prices as the cloud. Each production installation needs the self-hosted base, billed yearly: a commercial license with warranty, our builds with security fixes, and 12 support tickets a year, answered the next business day. Add-ons cost what they cost in the cloud, for each production installation; the installation counts its own usage and reports it monthly. Air-gapped installations settle their usage once a year, in an Enterprise contract. Zitadel is also open source: without the base you can run it under the AGPL 3.0 license, without warranty or support.

free.label: Pay as you go
free.over_allowance: Nothing is billed until an add-on is on, and no add-on turns on by itself. Owners get an email and a console banner at 50, 80 and 100 percent of each free amount, naming the add-on that lifts it. The first month past a free amount, nothing stops. From the next month, a meter still past its free amount without its add-on holds new usage: a social user or SSO connection not yet counted that month waits until the add-on is on. Service tokens, authorization checks, token exchanges and executions past it are slowed by a lower rate limit, never refused outright. Everyone already counted that month keeps signing in, and passwords, passkeys and MFA never stop.
